title: In 1871, a Fire Burned 1.2 Million Acres the Night Chicago Burned

scenes.text: America's deadliest fire struck the same night as the Great Chicago Fire.
On October 8th, 1871, a brush fire in Wisconsin exploded into a firestorm.
It burned about 1.2 million acres, an area bigger than Rhode Island.
Survivors said it roared like a tornado, and the town of Peshtigo was destroyed in about an hour.
Many people survived only by jumping into the river.
More than 1,200 people died, five times Chicago's toll. The bigger fire never made the history books.

description:
On October 8th, 1871, the Peshtigo Fire burned roughly 1.2 million acres of Wisconsin and killed more than 1,200 people.
It began the same day as the Great Chicago Fire and killed at least five times as many.
Had you heard of it?
first_comment: Had you ever heard of the Peshtigo Fire before this?
